title: What an owner's browser gets in the admin
grade_reasons: D, at the top of the band; I recomputed the figures from the build's own stats and they hold. Every one of the 432 signed-in screens loads about 1.15 MB of script where about 0.65 MB will do, 27 screens load an editor or a catalogue they never draw (up to 4.27 MB), every screen makes 23 to 46 requests nobody asked for, and a product editor's document is two thirds unread words; budgets watch 9 of 449 routes, about 4% above figures that already hold the waste, and none of the worst four. It is not an E, because nobody is hurt yet and most of the fix is import lines; it is not a C, because the state after phase 0 is what C describes (a sound base, real waste, some of it held) and today is plainly a grade worse.
verdict_on_bar: The floor first. React and Next are 447,102 bytes on all 560 routes, as the steward says (seven files, summed here). The frame is not 64 KB. I re-ran the cut simulation on the built chunks: a signed-in screen that is the frame alone (the account's Billing) lands at about 616,000 bytes, so the frame is about 169 KB. The 64 KB is only what leaves when one part is dropped. So 650,000 is the frame plus 34 KB of a screen's own code, not plus 140 KB. It is tighter than the steward believed and I keep it: about 200 KB gzip, of which 134 KB is the framework. Kept as well: 800,000 by idle on the home, the builder at 1,800,000 (about 1.6 MB by modules plus 12%; I could not check that floor closer than 100 KB either way), 0 prefetches at rest, 6 notice requests an hour, 100 rows a list, and Google's good line in production. Tightened in five places. (1) zod. 'At most 160 routes, on a list that may only shrink' is a B by the steward's own rule. Only 4 of 332 admin client files call a schema, and my re-run leaves zod on 118 screens outside the builder, brought by a helper that shares a file with a schema: 117 to 150 KB each. New bar: at most 60 routes, each named with the schema it runs. (2) A product's editor gets its own line, 1,100,000. Its only ceiling was 1,300,000, set where the cuts happen to land (about 1.26 MB), and about 290 KB of that is zod and the page model, which the screen's own code does not run. (3) The builder's document: 445,000, not 480,000. Step 2.30's own figure for its texts gives 439,000. (4) Requests at rest are held on eight screens, not on the home alone. The pages list (46) and settings (44) are today's worst. (5) By idle, the builder gets a number, 2,500,000. Step 2.29 moves 435 KB to after first paint and nothing counted it. Added: the words in Norwegian (45.3 KB shared today, against 34.0 in English), what a save sends back, a frame-alone figure, and a time figure in the lab until production has 100 loads a kind. Loosened: nothing. Not measurable as written: the steward's request budgets on orders, a product's editor and the builder have no step that creates them, and the production figure needs loads that do not exist before opening.

The store home 1,194,862 (360,861 gzip), orders 1,186,348, products 1,167,291, settings 1,140,078, the platform home 1,149,116. A screen that is the frame alone (the account's Billing) is 1,123,681. measures.name: Words a screen is handed, and what a save sends back
measures.today: Every store screen is handed 34.0 KB of shared words in English (45.3 KB in Norwegian) and reads about 12 KB. A product's editor is handed 238.5 KB and reads 78.9 KB. The builder is handed 311.6 KB and reads 195.4 KB. Documents: store home 165,942 characters, product editor 426,497 bytes (108 KB gzip), builder 585,943 (136 KB gzip). Each save or poll sends 51 to 66 KB of unchanged shell words again.
measures.target_a: At least 90% of the words handed are read on the five budgeted screens, in English and in Norwegian, and no screen is under 80%. Shared words at most 16 KB (17 KB in Norwegian). Documents: store home at or under 140,000 characters, product editor 290,000 bytes, builder 445,000 with a texts object of at most 130,000. A save answers with under 20 KB of words.

measures.name: Requests a screen makes when nobody touches it

At least 39 saves draw the whole route twice. One notice request per load and one a minute per visible tab: 60 requests and 240 statements an hour.

No second draw after a save. At most 6 notice requests an hour from an untouched tab, each at most 2 statements after the account read.

The ratchet's count of direct next/link imports (step 2.6). router-refresh.scan.test.ts (step 0.18). A clock case in e2e/signed-in/ai-manager-panel.spec.ts (step 2.34) and assistant-notices.int.test.ts (step 0.17).

measures.name: What grows with the store: rows on a list
measures.today: The Products list sends every product: about 0.9 KB of document a product, with no limit in listAdminProducts(). An estimated 4.5 MB at 5,000 products. The customers list groups every order before it cuts to 100, and the platform's Stores list loads every store. The test stores have 10 products, so nothing shows today.
measures.target_a: At most 100 rows a page on products, customers, stores and pages. A store with 500 products gets a Products document under 300,000 characters that says '100 of 500'.
measures.how_measured: The seeded case and the integration test of step 0.19; listPages() pages at 100 in step 2.17. The server area's card holds the reads behind them.

measures.name: What holds it, and the speed owners get
measures.today: 9 of 449 admin routes have a script budget, about 4% above figures that include the waste, and none of the worst four. No document, by-idle or request figure is held. The one production figure, the admin's own speed beacon, read 3.93 s LCP at p75 (INP 136 ms, TTFB 321 ms) over 52 loads on 29 and 30 October, when a plain screen loaded about 3.0 MB of script. It has not been read since, and nothing warns when it is not good. No lab figure of time exists for the admin.
measures.target_a: 449 of 449 routes in a baseline that only falls. Document, words, by-idle and request budgets on the budgeted screens in both languages. The import walk green. In production: LCP at p75 at or under 2.5 s and INP at or under 200 ms for every kind of admin screen with 100 loads or more in 28 days, with a line in the platform's briefing when one is not. Until a kind has 100 loads, a lab run with the processor slowed four times stands in: a plain screen paints within 2.5 s, and the two editors' figures are recorded and held.
measures.how_measured: scripts/bundle-budget.mjs in CI (step 1.2). admin-bundle.scan.test.ts (step 1.4). e2e/signed-in/admin-scripts.spec.ts and prefetch.spec.ts (steps 1.5 and 0.13). Platform, Usage and limits (commerce.own_speed_samples, site 'admin') and the briefing line of step 1.15. The lab run and the reading of the production table have no step yet (shortfall 3).

bar_in_a_sentence: A plain admin screen starts with at most 650 KB of script (447 KB of it is React and Next), a product's editor with at most 1.1 MB and the page builder with at most 1.8 MB; nothing is downloaded for a part the screen does not draw, nine tenths of the words handed to a screen are read, and a screen nobody touches asks the server for nothing but a notice count every ten minutes. Every route sits under a budget that only falls, and owners' real page loads paint within 2.5 seconds.
can_the_steps_reach_a: Not as written. Two numbers stop short, two checks are missing and three numbers reach with no room. The sums are from my re-run of the cut simulation on the built chunks, each route corrected by its gap to the build's stats. Plain screens: the median goes from 1,152,953 to about 648,330 after step 0.9, under 650,000 by 0.3%. The home goes to 687,662 and to 665,092 after step 2.26; orders 678,521; products 660,091; settings 632,251; the platform home 641,289. All are under 680,000, orders by 0.2% until its 14 KB of English goes. By idle: the home goes from 1,428,740 to about 947,000 after steps 0.9 and 0.13, about 925,000 after 2.26 and about 782,000 with the auth client alone (step 2.31). It reaches, with 2% to spare. The builder: 3,303,372 to about 3,044,000 (step 0.9), 2,256,753 (2.29) and 2,107,075 (2.26). Step 2.30 must then find 307,000. The parts it names are about 120,000 by the analyzer's module sizes: the dialogs about 40,000 and block-fields.tsx 81,000. As written it stops near 1,990,000, about 190,000 short. A product's editor: 2,130,796 to 1,323,497 after phase 0 and about 1,255,000 after steps 0.16 and 2.26, about 155,000 over its line. If step 0.10 also takes the page model off it (up to 172,000), it lands near 1,083,000 and reaches; no step's done-when says which. Not drawn: Supabase 432 routes to 0, the editor 73 to 0, a language 40 to 0, English copies 38 sites to 0, the chat 496,206 to 130,000: all reach. zod goes from 432 routes to about 144 and no step takes it lower: 84 routes short. Words: step 2.27's done-when is the bar, and it reaches. Requests: 28 to 0 on the home and 8 to 0 on the products rows (step 0.13); six of the eight screens are not counted. Polls: 60 an hour to 6 with the owner's yes (step 2.34). Speed: step 1.15 adds the alarm, but no step reads the figure, which was 3.93 s before any cut. One count in phase 0 does not hold: step 0.11 asks for at most 26 routes over 1,300,000, and a product's two editor routes sit at about 1,323,000 until step 2.26, so it reads 28. With the four shortfall steps and the owner's yes on the badge, every measure reaches its target and has a check. Without them the area ends at a B.

shortfalls.what: zod stays on about 144 routes, on a list that 'may only shrink', and no step shrinks it. Only 4 of 332 admin client files call a schema: the builder, the draft editor, the automation rule editor and the terms rules. On the other screens zod (116,870 bytes) and the schema modules beside it arrive because a helper or a constant shares a file with a schema: 118 screens outside the builder in my re-run, 117 to 150 KB each. A product's editor carries about 290 KB this way (zod and the page model) and ends between 1.08 and 1.26 MB against its line of 1.1 MB, with no step naming its figure.
shortfalls.proposed_step_title: Keep schemas apart from the helpers beside them, so zod loads only where a screen runs one
shortfalls.proposed_step_what: Phase 2, effort M to L. 145 files under src/lib import zod, and admin components import 67 of them directly (start with custom-fields.ts, 23 importers, and product-input.ts, 18; then theme.ts, motion.ts, visibility.ts, colour.ts and typography.ts). Where a client part takes only a helper or a constant, move the schema into a file of its own beside it, as step 0.9 does for push.ts and as the storefront already requires. The import walk of step 1.4 then lets zod be reached only from a named list of client modules, each with the schema it runs. Do the product editor first. The first act is the list itself: about 30 routes are shown to run a schema today, and 60 leaves room for screens whose library call parses.
shortfalls.proposed_done_when: After a build, 'ZodError' is in the first-load chunks of at most 60 routes (432 today, about 144 after step 0.9). /admin/[store]/products/[productId] is at or under 1,100,000 bytes in route-bundle-stats.json (2,130,796 today). admin-bundle.scan.test.ts names each client module that may reach zod with its schema, and fails for a new one.

shortfalls.what: Step 2.30 cannot reach its own number with the parts it names. After steps 0.9, 2.26 and 2.29 the builder stands at about 2,107,000 bytes. The dialogs the step names are about 40,000 bytes built and block-fields.tsx is 81,000: about 120,000 against the 307,000 needed. It would stop near 1,990,000. Its done-when also names no figure for the builder's document or for what the builder has loaded by idle, where step 2.29 leaves 435 KB that only moved.
shortfalls.proposed_step_title: Name the rest of the builder's last 307 KB before step 2.30 starts
shortfalls.proposed_step_what: Amend step 2.30. Load the whole settings panel when a part is first selected, not only each block's form: page-builder-fields.tsx (45,000 bytes built) and the display, motion, typography, modal, font and colour fields (77,000). Load the custom-fields form and the terms manager when they are opened (50,000), and the brand icon list (25,000) if only the icon picker needs it. With the cookie table of step 0.16 (24,000) the list is about 340,000, or 315,000 without the icons. First run the cut simulation with these import edges removed and write its table into the step. If it sums under 310,000, the builder's own split (code review step 3.1) joins the step.
shortfalls.proposed_done_when: The step holds the simulation's table, summing to at least 310,000 bytes, before work starts. Then /admin/[store]/pages/[pageId] is at or under 1,800,000 bytes in route-bundle-stats.json, its document is at or under 445,000 bytes, the builder's script by idle is at or under 2,500,000 in the by-idle budget of e2e/signed-in/admin-scripts.spec.ts (3,454,740 today), and the signed-in builder specs pass.

shortfalls.what: Requests at rest are held on two screens and time on none. Step 0.13's spec counts the home and the products rows. The pages list (46 prefetches) and settings (44) are today's worst and are not in it, and 335 admin files import next/link directly. Step 1.15 adds an alarm for the production figure, but its done-when is a unit test: no step reads the figure (3.93 s before any cut, against 2.5 s), and before opening only the team's own loads exist. No lab figure of time exists for the admin.
shortfalls.proposed_step_title: Hold requests at rest on the eight budgeted screens, and give the admin a time figure before owners arrive
shortfalls.proposed_step_what: Phase 1, effort M. Add to steps 0.13, 1.5 and 1.15. e2e/signed-in/prefetch.spec.ts keeps one table for eight screens (home, orders, products, pages, settings, a product's editor, the builder, the platform home): the router prefetches in the 3 seconds after load, and the page's own fetches after load, each named. The slowed run that step 1.14 adds for shoppers also loads the home, orders, a product's editor and the builder, signed in, at desktop width with the processor slowed four times, and records largest paint, blocking time and the script run by idle. Read the production table when phase 0 has been live for 28 days and again after phase 2, and write both into docs/performance.md. A kind that is not good gets a step that says where its time goes. The bar does not move.
shortfalls.proposed_done_when: prefetch.spec.ts passes with 0 router prefetches at rest on all eight screens (23 to 46 today) and no fetch after load but the notice count and the builder's named start calls. docs/performance.md holds the slowed run's four admin figures, with the home and orders painting within 2.5 s and the script run by idle held within 5%. It also holds the 28-day production table after phase 0 and after phase 2, with every kind of 100 loads or more at LCP 2.5 s and INP 200 ms or better.

shortfalls.what: Three numbers reach their bar with no room, and one count in phase 0 does not hold. The median lands at about 648,330 against 650,000 (0.3%). Orders lands at 678,521 against 680,000. Step 0.11 asks for at most 26 routes over 1,300,000 at the end of phase 0, but a product's two editor routes sit at about 1,323,000 until step 2.26, so the count is 28.
shortfalls.proposed_step_title: Give the thin numbers room: sign-in's words out of the frame, and the product editor's English with step 0.10
shortfalls.proposed_step_what: Effort S, inside steps 0.9 and 0.10. Sign-in's English (about 8 KB built) is in the first scripts of 442 admin routes and is read by two parts, the two-step panel and the recovery codes. Load it with those two parts and on the sign-in pages only. Do the product editor's English sites (fields and redirects, about 43,000 bytes) and the move of the rich text types out of page-content.ts (the fifth fix step of AC-3) inside step 0.10, not in phase 2.
shortfalls.proposed_done_when: After a build, the marker 'Use a recovery code' is in the first-load chunks of at most 20 routes (442 today), the median admin route is at or under 645,000 bytes, and at the end of phase 0 at most 26 routes are over 1,300,000 bytes, with /admin/[store]/products/[productId] under that line.

tolerated: React and Next: 447,102 bytes (134 KB gzip) in every screen's first scripts. It cannot go.

The admin's frame: about 169 KB on every signed-in screen. It is the rail and its icons, the menus, shortcuts, tooltips, the colour scheme, the AI manager's launcher, and the common and sign-in words in English (about 15 KB).
15,000 bytes of room a route in the script baseline, about 2% of a plain screen.
Supabase's auth client alone, about 117 KB, after the page is idle, if the trial of step 2.31 keeps it. It refreshes the session and is off the first paint.
The rich text editor, 435 KB, arrives in the builder after first paint on every open. Editing text is the builder's main job.
The builder at 1.8 MB: about 12% over what its modules need, an estimate that could be 100 KB out either way.
zod (117 KB) on the builder's 26 routes and on at most 34 other screens whose own code runs a schema.
Up to 10% of the words handed to a screen go unread. The builder's own words (about 130 KB) travel inside each document and are not cached; a save sends under 20 KB of them again.
The notice badge asks at most 6 times an hour from a tab nobody touches, so a notice can be ten minutes late there.
A touch or a keyboard press on an admin link shows the pending bar for one round trip, because links are fetched when pointed at.

Second copies of modules across chunks: 40% of the built client files, of which a browser meets about 14% while moving around. It is the chunker's trade. Measure again after the cuts, and adopt Next's flag only if a 59-screen tour falls by 10% or more.
The admin's two stylesheets, 204 KB raw (about 36 KB gzip). The styles area holds them.
owner_choices: May the notice badge in a tab nobody touches be up to ten minutes late (60 requests an hour become 6)? It shows at once on the next click and stays at one minute while an approval waits. Without this yes the poll stays at 60 an hour, at two statements each, and that number becomes the stated tolerance.
The Products, Customers and Stores lists will show 100 rows at a time. Should 'select all' and a bulk action reach every row that matches, or only the 100 on the screen?

Step 2.31 keeps the session one of two ways, by trial: the auth client alone (117 KB after idle, nothing else changes) or a small refresh route (0 KB). The second changes a written sign-in rule: tokens are refreshed in the browser today. Do you want to be asked before that rule changes?
